newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway economic growth set to slow - OECD.
newsitem.headline: Norway economic growth set to slow - OECD.

text.p: Norway's mainland economic growth is expected to taper off over the next two years with domestic demand forecast to expand only moderately and non-oil exports to progressively lose competitiveness, the OECD said on Thursday.

In a half-year outlook, the OECD forecast a slowdown in growth in Norway's mainland gross domestic product (GDP) from an estimated 3.4 percent this year to 2.5 percent in 1997 and two percent in 1998.
The Paris-based body said that despite the continued cyclic rebound in the labour supply, GDP growth should suffice to reduce unemployment to 3.6 percent by the end of 1998 from 4.2 percent in 1996.

It sounded a warning note over the risk to the Norwegian economy of wage and price inflation brought on by the tightness of the current labour market and growing calls for rises in public expenditure.

"With labour market conditions thus tightening, wage growth is projected to accelerate to over five percent and consumer price inflation, after attaining 1.5 percent in 1996, could creep up to around 2.5 percent by 1998," the report said.
It said that as oil and gas exports stabilised at current historic high levels, overall GDP growth should slow down from five percent this year to 2.5 percent at the end of the forecast period.
According to figures from government department Statistics Norway, oil and gas accounted for 50 percent of exports in the period January to November 1996.
The OECD said an assumed correction of the recent oil price rise should limit any further rise in Norway's current account surplus to just over six percent of GDP.
